key_insight: In a small randomized placebo-controlled phase I trial, an oral fungal mycelial combination (FoTv) appeared safe and feasible for mild-to-moderate COVID-19, with exploratory signals for symptom reduction and lower inflammatory markers.
clinical_relevance: This early study suggests FoTv could be a low-cost, at-home adjunct approach worth further testing, but it is not yet established as a treatment.
method: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase I trial at two sites (UCSD/UCLA)
50 non-hospitalized participants with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 (26 FoTv, 24 placebo)
Safety labs, adherence, symptoms, CRP, and in vitro pseudovirus infection were assessed
evidence_signal: Across the trial, renal, hepatic, and coagulation markers stayed within normal ranges, adherence was high, and exploratory analyses showed symptom and CRP improvements plus reduced pseudovirus cellular infection in vitro.
watch_item: Findings are preliminary and based on a small sample with exploratory outcomes, so efficacy and generalizability remain uncertain.
paper_title: Safety, Feasibility, and Preliminary Clinical Findings of an Oral Polypore Fungi Combination with Mild-to-Moderate COVID-19: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Phase I Clinical Trial
